added_lemmas.statement:
Assume the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask conditions, \(\mu=1\), \(0<\kappa\le 1\), and \(0<s_-\le s_+\).  Then both normalized overlap Grams in the unique balanced chart equal \(1\), so the value of \(\kappa\) does not further restrict this boundary class.  For all sufficiently large even \(n\), the minimax expected honest radius has the following complete boundary characterization.
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
s_-<s_+:& c_\alpha\sigma\le \rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\le C_\alpha\sigma,
\quad\text{hence }\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma,\\[3pt]
s_-=s_+:& \rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}=0,
\end{array}
\]
where \(0<c_\alpha<C_\alpha<\infty\) depend only on \(\alpha\).  The first upper bound and the zero-radius result are attained by deterministic \(O(n^2)\)-time procedures in \(\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\); in the second line the common factor level is known because the parameter-space constants coincide.  In both cases
\[
\mathfrak R_n\ge \sigma\sqrt{2n}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\frac{\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}}{\mathfrak R_n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently, no positive constant can make an all-procedure inequality \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\ge c\mathfrak R_n\) hold over every parameter choice and wedge allowed by the model.  The obstruction is that at \(\mu=1\) the admissible rank-one singular vectors have only coordinatewise sign choices, whereas the unrestricted rank-manifold tangent space still contains continuous directions.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(n=2m\).  By the balanced-dimension, even-benchmark, balanced-L-mask, and one-chart assumptions, the unique chart has
\[
C=P=\{1,\ldots,m\},\qquad I=Q=\{m+1,\ldots,2m\},
\]
and
\[
W_n=I\times Q,qquad
\Omega_n=(C\times P)\mathbin{\sqcup}(I\times P)
\mathbin{\sqcup}(C\times Q),qquad |\Omega_n|=3m^2.       \tag{1}
\]

We first identify the entire \(\mu=1\) boundary class.  The rank-one and strong-factor assumptions give, for every \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\in\Theta_n\), a singular-value decomposition
\[
L_n=s_nu_nv_n^{\top},\qquad
\lVert u_n\rVert_2=\lVert v_n\rVert_2=1,qquad
s_-n\le s_n\le s_+n.                                      \tag{2}
\]
At \(\mu=1\), incoherence says
\[
|u_{n,i}|^2\le n^{-1}\quad(1\le i\le n),
\qquad |v_{n,t}|^2\le n^{-1}\quad(1\le t\le n).          \tag{3}
\]
The \(n\) nonnegative quantities on each side of (3) sum to one.  Thus every inequality in (3) is an equality.  Hence there are signs \(p_i,q_t\in\{-1,1\}\) and a level
\(\ell_n=s_n/n\in[s_-,s_+]\) such that
\[
u_{n,i}=\frac{p_i}{\sqrt n},\qquad
v_{n,t}=\frac{q_t}{\sqrt n},\qquad
L_{n,it}=\ell_np_iq_t.                                    \tag{4}
\]
The normalized row and column Grams in the unique balanced chart are well defined because \(|C|=|P|=m>0\), and (4) yields
\[
\frac{n}{|C|}u_{n,C}^{\top}u_{n,C}
=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{i\in C}\frac1n=1,
\qquad
\frac{n}{|P|}v_{n,P}^{\top}v_{n,P}
=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{t\in P}\frac1n=1.                     \tag{5}
\]
Thus every boundary matrix satisfies the overlap-Gram restriction for every \(0<\kappa\le1\), not merely for \(\kappa=1\).

We next preserve the lower bound for the geometric modulus.  The class is nonempty: take \(p_i=q_t=1\), \(\ell_n=s_-\), and \(D_n=0\).  Equations (2)--(5), together with treatment support, verify membership in \(\Theta_n\).  For this matrix let \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_n)^{\top}\), and take any vector \(h\in\mathbb R^n\) supported on \(I\).  Since \(v_n=q/\sqrt n\),
\[
\Delta=hq^{\top}=(\sqrt n\,h)v_n^{\top}\in\mathcal T_n(L_n)          \tag{6}
\]
by the definition of the tangent space.  The decomposition (1) and the support of \(h\) give
\[
\lVert P_{\Omega_n}\Delta\rVert_F
=\lVert h_Iq_P^{\top}\rVert_F
=\sqrt m\,\lVert h\rVert_2,
\qquad
\lVert P_{W_n}\Delta\rVert_*
=\lVert h_Iq_Q^{\top}\rVert_*
=\sqrt m\,\lVert h\rVert_2.                              \tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the only nonzero singular value of a rank-one matrix \(ab^{\top}\) is
\(\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert b\rVert_2\), which proves the nuclear-norm equality in (7).  Choose \(h\) so that \(\sqrt m\lVert h\rVert_2=\sigma\sqrt{2n}\).  Since \(r=1\) and \(N_n=T_n=n\), this \(\Delta\) is feasible in the definition of \(\omega_n(L_n,\Omega_n)\).  Therefore
\[
\mathfrak R_n\ge \omega_n(L_n,\Omega_n)
\ge\sigma\sqrt{2n}.                                      \tag{8}
\]

We now construct a common relative-sign pilot.  Fix \(i_0\in C\), \(t_0\in P\), set \(\operatorname{sign}(0)=1\), and define from observed cells only
\[
\widehat p_i=\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\sum_{t\in P}X_{n,it}X_{n,i_0t}\right),
\qquad
\widehat q_t=\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\sum_{i\in C}X_{n,it}X_{n,it_0}\right).       \tag{9}
\]
All cells used in (9) lie in \(\Omega_n\) by (1).  Treatment support and the observed-experiment definition therefore give \(X_{n,it}=L_{n,it}+E_{n,it}\) at each such cell.  For \(i\ne i_0\), multiplication of the row score in (9) by \(p_ip_{i_0}\), followed by sign invariance of centered Gaussian errors, gives the distributional identity
\[
S_i=\sum_{t=1}^{m}(\ell_n+\varepsilon_t)(\ell_n+\delta_t)
=m\ell_n^2+G_i+H_i,                                      \tag{10}
\]
where the pairs \((\varepsilon_t,\delta_t)\) are independent over \(t\), their two coordinates are independent \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) variables, and
\[
G_i=\ell_n\sum_{t=1}^{m}(\varepsilon_t+\delta_t)
\sim\mathcal N(0,2m\ell_n^2\sigma^2),
\qquad H_i=\sum_{t=1}^{m}\varepsilon_t\delta_t.           \tag{11}
\]
For \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,v)\), exponential Markov inequality and minimization over \(a>0\) give
\[
\Pr(G\le-x)\le\inf_{a>0}\exp\{-ax+a^2v/2\}
=\exp\{-x^2/(2v)\}.                                     \tag{12}
\]
Applying (12) to (11) yields
\[
\Pr\!\left(G_i\le-\frac{m\ell_n^2}{2}\right)
\le\exp\!\left\{-\frac{m\ell_n^2}{16\sigma^2}\right\}.             \tag{13}
\]
For \(0<a<\sigma^{-2}\), conditioning on one Gaussian and integrating the other gives
\[
\mathbb E\exp(-a\varepsilon_t\delta_t)
=(1-\sigma^4a^2)^{-1/2}.                                 \tag{14}
\]
If \(0<a\le(2\sigma^2)^{-1}\), then
\(-\tfrac12\log(1-\sigma^4a^2)\le\sigma^4a^2\).  Independence, (14), and exponential Markov inequality imply
\[
\Pr\!\left(H_i\le-\frac{m\ell_n^2}{2}\right)
\le\exp\!\left\{-\frac{ma\ell_n^2}{2}+m\sigma^4a^2\right\}.         \tag{15}
\]
Taking \(a=\min\{\ell_n^2/(4\sigma^4),(2\sigma^2)^{-1}\}\), and using \(\ell_n\ge s_->0\), gives
\[
\Pr\!\left(H_i\le-\frac{m\ell_n^2}{2}\right)\le e^{-mc_2},
\quad
c_2=\min\!\left\{\frac{s_-^4}{16\sigma^4},\frac14\right\}>0.       \tag{16}
\]
If \(S_i\le0\), either event in (13) and (16) occurs.  Thus, with
\[
c_1=\frac{s_-^2}{16\sigma^2},
\qquad c_\star=\min\{c_1,c_2\}>0,
\]
we have
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}}\{\widehat p_i\ne p_ip_{i_0}\}
\le e^{-mc_1}+e^{-mc_2}\quad(i\ne i_0).                  \tag{17}
\]
For \(i=i_0\), the row score is a sum of squares and is positive almost surely.  The identical argument with rows and columns interchanged proves (17) for \(\widehat q_t\ne q_tq_{t_0}\), while the reference-column score is again positive almost surely.  Consequently the event
\[
\mathcal S_n=
\{\widehat p_i=p_ip_{i_0}\ \text{for all }i,
\ \widehat q_t=q_tq_{t_0}\ \text{for all }t\}
\]
satisfies the uniform bound
\[
\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}
\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}(\mathcal S_n^c)
\le2(n-1)(e^{-mc_1}+e^{-mc_2})
\le4ne^{-mc_\star}.                                      \tag{18}
\]
No independence among the comparisons is used in this union bound.

Suppose first that \(s_-<s_+\).  Let \(\Phi\) denote the standard-normal distribution function and put \(z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/4)\).  Define
\[
\widehat\ell_n=\frac1{3m^2}\sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_n}
X_{n,it}\widehat p_i\widehat q_t,
\qquad
\widehat L_{n,it}=\widehat\ell_n\widehat p_i\widehat q_t,
\qquad
R_n=\frac{z_\alpha}{\sqrt3}\sigma.                       \tag{19}
\]
On \(\mathcal S_n\), let \(c=p_{i_0}q_{t_0}\).  Then
\(\widehat p_i\widehat q_t=cp_iq_t\), and (4), (19), and the independent Gaussian-cell assumption give
\[
\widehat\ell_n=c(\ell_n+Z_n),
\qquad
Z_n=\frac1{3m^2}\sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_n}p_iq_tE_{n,it}
\sim\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{\sigma^2}{3m^2}\right).                \tag{20}
\]
It follows that on \(\mathcal S_n\),
\[
P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)=Z_np_Iq_Q^{\top},
\qquad
\lVert P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)\rVert_*=m|Z_n|.          \tag{21}
\]
By the definition of \(z_\alpha\),
\[
\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n}\{m|Z_n|>R_n\}=\alpha/2.          \tag{22}
\]
For all sufficiently large even \(n\), the right side of (18) is at most \(\alpha/2\).  Combining (18), (21), and (22), without requiring independence between \(\mathcal S_n\) and \(Z_n\), proves
\[
\inf_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}
\Pr_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}
\{\lVert P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L_n)\rVert_*\le R_n\}
\ge1-\alpha.                                               \tag{23}
\]
Thus (19) belongs to \(\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\).  Its two families of correlations, its signed average, and its outer-product completion require \(O(n^2)\) arithmetic operations.  Since \(R_n\) is deterministic, the minimax definition gives
\[
\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\le \frac{z_\alpha}{\sqrt3}\sigma.           \tag{24}
\]

For the matching all-procedure lower bound, retain the fixed signs \(p_i=q_t=1\).  Set
\[
a_\alpha=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2\sqrt3}>0,
\qquad
\delta_n=\frac{a_\alpha\sigma}{m},
\qquad
\ell_0=s_-,\qquad \ell_1=s_-+\delta_n.                  \tag{25}
\]
Because \(s_-<s_+\), one has \(\ell_1\le s_+\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Let
\(L^{(j)}=\ell_j\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^{\top}\) and \(D^{(j)}=0\) for \(j=0,1\).  Equations (2)--(5) and treatment support show that both tuples belong to \(\Theta_n\).  Their level separation is \(a_\alpha\sigma/m\), as required, and their observed Gaussian means differ by \(\delta_n\) in each of the \(3m^2\) coordinates of \(\Omega_n\).

Let \(f_0,f_1\) be the two observed Gaussian densities.  Completing the square coordinatewise gives their Hellinger affinity
\[
A:=\int\sqrt{f_0f_1}
=\exp\!\left\{-\frac{\lVert
\operatorname{vec}_{\Omega_n}(L^{(1)}-L^{(0)})\rVert_2^2}{8\sigma^2}\right\}
=\exp\!\left\{-\frac{3a_\alpha^2}{8}\right\}.           \tag{26}
\]
Writing total variation as one half of the \(L^1\) distance and applying Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1)
&=\frac12\int|\sqrt{f_0}-\sqrt{f_1}|(\sqrt{f_0}+\sqrt{f_1})\\
&\le\frac12\{(2-2A)(2+2A)\}^{1/2}
=\sqrt{1-A^2}\\
&\le\frac{\sqrt3a_\alpha}{2}
=\frac{1-2\alpha}{4}.                                    \tag{27}
\end{aligned}
\]
The penultimate inequality follows from \(1-e^{-x}\le x\) for \(x\ge0\).  Adjoining the common independent laws of \(\Xi_n\) and \(\Zeta_n\) leaves total variation unchanged, because integration over the common product factor multiplies the \(L^1\) distance by one.

Take any \((\widehat L_n,R_n)\in\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\), and under the joint law associated with tuple \(j\) define
\[
\mathcal A_j=
\{\lVert P_{W_n}(\widehat L_n-L^{(j)})\rVert_*\le R_n\}.
\]
Uniform honesty gives \(\Pr_j(\mathcal A_j)\ge1-\alpha\).  By (27),
\[
\Pr_0(\mathcal A_0\cap\mathcal A_1)
\ge1-2\alpha-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1)
\ge\frac34(1-2\alpha).                                   \tag{28}
\]
On this intersection, the triangle inequality for the nuclear norm gives
\[
2R_n\ge\lVert P_{W_n}(L^{(1)}-L^{(0)})\rVert_*
=\delta_n\lVert\mathbf1_I\mathbf1_Q^{\top}\rVert_*
=m\delta_n=a_\alpha\sigma.                               \tag{29}
\]
Therefore
\[
\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}[R_n]
\ge\mathbb E_0R_n
\ge\frac{3a_\alpha(1-2\alpha)}8\sigma
=\frac{3(1-2\alpha)^2}{16\sqrt3}\sigma.                 \tag{30}
\]
Taking the infimum over all honest procedures in (30), and combining with (24), proves the asserted \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\) characterization.  Notice that (25)--(30) use two fixed-sign matrices and vary only their positive factor level; the treatment-effect component is fixed at zero, and no causal treatment effect is identified by definition.

It remains to treat the elbow \(s_-=s_+\).  Write the known common value as \(s_0:=s_-=s_+>0\).  Use the same relative signs (9), and set
\[
\overline X_n^{\mathrm{sgn}}
=\frac1{3m^2}\sum_{(i,t)\in\Omega_n}X_{n,it}\widehat p_i\widehat q_t,
\qquad
\widehat c_n=\operatorname{sign}(\overline X_n^{\mathrm{sgn}}),
\]
\[
\widehat L_{n,it}=s_0\widehat c_n\widehat p_i\widehat q_t,
\qquad R_n=0.                                              \tag{31}
\]
On \(\mathcal S_n\), equation (20) becomes
\[
\overline X_n^{\mathrm{sgn}}=c(s_0+Z_n),
\qquad Z_n\sim\mathcal N\!\left(0,\frac{\sigma^2}{3m^2}\right).     \tag{32}
\]
Thus \(\widehat c_n=c\) whenever \(\mathcal S_n\) occurs and \(Z_n>-s_0\), and then (31) equals \(L_n\) at every cell.  Applying the elementary Gaussian bound (12) to (32),
\[
\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}
\Pr\{P_{W_n}\widehat L_n\ne P_{W_n}L_n\}
\le4ne^{-mc_\star}
+\exp\!\left\{-\frac{3m^2s_0^2}{2\sigma^2}\right\}.     \tag{33}
\]
The right side is at most \(\alpha\) for all sufficiently large even \(n\).  Hence the deterministic \(O(n^2)\)-time pair (31) lies in \(\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\).  Its radius is identically zero.  Since every admissible radius is nonnegative by definition,
\[
0\le\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\le0,                         \tag{34}
\]
which proves \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}=0\).

Finally, (8) and (24) give in the nondegenerate case
\[
0\le\frac{\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}}{\mathfrak R_n}
\le\frac{z_\alpha}{\sqrt{6n}}\longrightarrow0,           \tag{35}
\]
while the ratio is identically zero in the known-level case by (34).  This proves the universal lower-comparison obstruction.  Equations (4) and (6) also isolate its source: the active incoherence boundary makes admissible singular-vector magnitudes fixed, but the tangent modulus still optimizes over directions that do not remain in that boundary class.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem gives the full saturated-incoherence boundary frontier, including the exact known-level elbow, and proves why the unrestricted tangent modulus is not a same-class minimax lower benchmark there.
added_lemmas.gap: The fixed-\(\mu>1\) interior theorem has order \(\sigma\sqrt n\), but it does not cover the active boundary \(\mu=1\); the boundary instead has order \(\sigma\) for a nondegenerate level interval and zero radius for a known singleton level.
added_lemmas.consumer: Researchers can choose the correct honest-radius scale at the saturated boundary and avoid extrapolating either the fixed-interior frontier or the unrestricted tangent modulus to \(\mu=1\).

added_lemmas.statement: Determine the minimax order of \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\) in the two regimes not settled by the boundary and fixed-interior theorems: first, the balanced rank-one L-mask when the incoherence bound is allowed to depend on \(n\), with \(\mu=\mu(n)>1\) and \(\mu(n)\downarrow1\); second, arbitrary quantitatively admissible interior multi-chart wedges with fixed \(\mu>1\) and \(0<\kappa\le1\).  In each regime, determine whether a polynomial-time uniformly honest spectral certificate and a same-class all-procedure lower bound match.  No interpolation rate between the zero/\(\sigma\) boundary frontier and the fixed-interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier is asserted.
added_lemmas.justification: The proved endpoints leave two mathematically distinct problems: the shrinking layer next to active incoherence and the geometry of arbitrary interior multi-chart wedges.
added_lemmas.gap: Neither the boundary sign experiment nor the fixed-\(\mu>1\) one-block packing supplies a uniform interpolation theorem or a matching arbitrary-wedge certificate.
added_lemmas.consumer: A solution would tell panel researchers when boundary discreteness ceases to dominate and whether general staggered wedges admit a computationally matched honest-radius frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: Characterize separately the shrinking-incoherence boundary layer and the fixed-interior arbitrary multi-chart wedge frontier, with matching honest upper and all-procedure lower bounds when possible.
obligation.obstruction: The boundary proof uses discrete sign recovery once incoherence is exactly active, whereas the interior proof uses continuous perturbations with slack. Neither argument is uniform as the slack vanishes, and no same-class tangent packing is available for every admissible multi-chart wedge.
obligation.attempted: The exact \(\mu=1\) reduction and the fixed-\(\mu>1\) one-block frontier determine the two endpoint regimes, but they do not determine an interpolation scale or control chart synchronization and mask amplification uniformly over general wedges.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old theorem records only the \(\mu=\kappa=1\) upper-bound obstruction. The replacement proves the strictly stronger full \(\mu=1\), arbitrary \(0<\kappa\le1\) characterization, including the nondegenerate \(\Theta(\sigma)\) lower bound and the known-level zero-radius elbow. A replacement node is required because claim text may not be broadened through a statement-replace operation.

proposed.name: Note-specific single-baseline admissible tuple parameter space

proposed_core_edits.reason: The member set is unchanged, but the name now makes its positioning explicit: this is the note's one-baseline global-incoherence class, not Yan--Wainwright's two-potential-outcome-matrix class with two-sided subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise, and target-local leverage conditions. The literature relationship is an embedded-subclass converse transfer, not class identity or transfer of their construction.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 study two low-rank potential-outcome matrices under two-sided observed-subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and target-local leverage conditions, without imposing this note's global incoherence condition; they give entrywise Gaussian inference and a matching scalar instance-wise lower bound.
proposed.matched_by: Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier}, converse comparison only through an embedded subclass; the constructive bounds remain specific to this note's class

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorems 1 and 4 derive nuclear detection boundaries and nuclear-diameter rank-adaptation impossibility in Gaussian trace regression.
Theorems 3.4--3.5 characterize worst-case Frobenius residual error for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block.
Proposition 2 derives tall-wide common-component error expansions under strong factors in the observed subblocks.
The paper constructs prescribed-coverage intervals for individual effects and bilinear functionals under staggered adoption.
The paper gives rate-optimal recovery and asymptotic normality for average treatment effects under general intervention patterns.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement records the non-identity of the two parameter classes and limits the Yan--Wainwright transfer to the converse through an embedded subclass; it does not attribute this note's constructive nuclear-radius bounds to their assumptions.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper indexes the Gaussian panel experiment by admissible tuples \(\vartheta_n=(L_n,D_n)\), so the latent counterfactual matrix remains part of the experiment index even when tuples induce the same observed law. The balanced rank-one L-mask has a sharp phase split. For each fixed \(\mu>1\), Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} gives the all-procedure and polynomial-time frontier \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\sqrt n\). At the saturated boundary \(\mu=1\), both normalized overlap Grams equal one for every \(0<\kappa\le1\): Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} proves \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\asymp\sigma\) when \(s_-<s_+\), but \(\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}=0\) when the common level \(s_-=s_+\) is known. The unrestricted tangent modulus nevertheless remains at least \(\sigma\sqrt{2n}\), so it cannot support a uniform same-class lower comparison at the boundary. Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge} separates the shrinking-incoherence layer from the arbitrary interior multi-chart wedge frontier without asserting an interpolation rate. The diffuse-weight ATT interval remains only a coverage-valid nuclear/operator-duality corollary.

project_justification.gap: Sharp staggered-panel inference is usually coordinatewise or functional-specific, while global matrix confidence theory typically uses random or isotropic measurements. No located result gives a tuple-indexed honest nuclear ball under a deterministic adoption wedge together with both the fixed-interior frontier and the saturated-incoherence boundary elbow. Yan and Wainwright's two-potential-outcome-matrix class uses two-sided subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise, and target-local leverage conditions rather than this note's global incoherence class, so only a converse can transfer upward from an embedded subclass; their construction does not establish the present upper bounds.
project_justification.niche: Known rank, independent Gaussian cells, strong factors, and quantitative overlap Grams isolate a deterministic-wedge confidence problem with a genuine boundary phase change. In the balanced rank-one L-mask, fixed \(\mu>1\) permits continuous factor perturbations and a \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, whereas \(\mu=1\) fixes all singular-vector magnitudes, makes overlap automatically exact for every \(\kappa\le1\), and leaves only signs and the factor level to learn.
project_justification.fill: Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} retains the fixed-\(\mu>1\) \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier and its total polynomial-time spectral certificate. Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} gives the full \(\mu=1\) boundary frontier: an explicit polynomial-time honest radius of order \(\sigma\), a fixed-sign two-level all-procedure lower bound when \(s_-<s_+\), exact zero radius when the common level is known, and the simultaneous lower bound \(\mathfrak R_n\ge\sigma\sqrt{2n}\). Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge} leaves only the shrinking-incoherence layer and the arbitrary interior multi-chart frontier open.

sampling_model.design: The schedule \(g_n\), wedge \(\Omega_n\), dimensions, rank, noise variance, and class constants are fixed and known. The fixed-\(\mu>1\) rate-optimal spectral theorem and the separate \(\mu=1\) sign-based boundary theorem are both restricted to the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask.
sampling_model.overlap: The full class imposes quantitative observed-subblock Grams. In the unique balanced chart at \(\mu=1\), every singular-vector coordinate has squared magnitude \(1/n\), so both normalized overlap Grams equal one and every \(0<\kappa\le1\) defines the same boundary class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For fixed \(\mu>1\), the total spectral procedure uses independent Gaussian pilot and inference copies, total pseudoinverse conventions, one-step block transport, an ordered conditional Gaussian nuclear quantile, a homogeneous observable remainder, and a deterministic fallback; its \(\sigma\sqrt n\) guarantee is not asserted at \(\mu=1\). At \(\mu=1\), a separate deterministic \(O(n^2)\) procedure recovers row and column relative signs exponentially accurately, estimates the unknown level by a signed average when \(s_-<s_+\), and uses the known level with zero radius when \(s_-=s_+\).

prose_updates.related_work: Yan and Wainwright provide the closest computational and inferential comparison, but their model has two low-rank potential-outcome matrices, two-sided observed-subblock conditioning, signal-to-noise and target-local leverage conditions, and no global incoherence condition. Their class is therefore not identical to \(\Theta_n\): only the converse transfers upward through an embedded subclass, while the present constructive nuclear-radius bounds remain specific to this note's class. Bai and Ng supply tall-wide factor-rotation expansions under strong observed subblocks. Carpentier and Nickl study honest nuclear confidence diameter in isotropic Gaussian trace regression, where rank adaptation is the central obstruction. Capponi and Stojnic analyze worst-case Frobenius residuals for nuclear-norm minimization with one missing block. Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan treat debiased uncertainty quantification under random sampling, and Chatterjee gives qualitative recoverability under arbitrary deterministic masks. Against these comparators, Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier} supplies the fixed-\(\mu>1\) interior \(\sigma\sqrt n\) frontier, while Theorem \ref{thm:boundary-frontier-obstruction} proves the \(\mu=1\), arbitrary-\(\kappa\) \(\sigma\)-or-zero boundary frontier and the failure of the unrestricted tangent-modulus lower comparison. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright and Farias, Li, and Peng remain functional-specific benchmarks; the ATT proposition claims coverage transfer and no optimal-length comparison.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The \(\sigma\sqrt n\) certificate and packing theorem remain confined to fixed \(\mu>1\) in the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask. The new boundary proof is also benchmark-specific: it uses the exact \(\mu=1\) reduction to equal-magnitude singular vectors and the resulting rank-one sign experiment. It neither supplies a rate uniform over \(\mu=\mu(n)\downarrow1\) nor controls arbitrary connected multi-chart wedges. A broader result would need a uniform post-synchronization envelope and nuclear-mask amplification bound together with a same-class packing that preserves exact rank, strong factors, incoherence, overlap, and controlled observed-law divergence. Those are the two separate tasks in Open-ended Question \ref{oeq:boundary-layer-and-general-wedge}; no interpolation exponent is currently claimed.
